basis: Defined by congenital deafness, upper-limb malformations and pigmentary abnormalities; iris pigmentation does not impair vision; atelectasis lacks evidence of persistent damage.
Infection defines this umbrella; no anatomical organ is affected across most infectious diseases.
Defined by craniosynostosis and polysyndactyly; additional organ damage is subtype-dependent.
Thoracic/limb skeletal dysplasia; cerebellar malformation in 3/4 with developmental delay; pituitary hypoplasia in 2/4. Neonatal respiratory distress alone does not establish lasting lung damage.
Dermatofibrosarcoma arising in dermal and subcutaneous tissue; pigmentation does not change its organ of origin.
GH excess; structural arthropathy, persistent skin thickening/dermatitis and tongue hypertrophy each reported in 80-99%; hypertension is separately coded.
The defining abnormalities are folded skin, acanthosis nigricans and premature fusion of skull sutures.
Inherited isolated nail abnormalities; the definition excludes a broader multisystem syndrome.
Congenital two-chambered heart; the cardiac malformation defines the disease.
Spondylometaphyseal skeletal dysplasia with characteristic Pelger-Huet neutrophil hyposegmentation, reported in 2/2; this does not imply immunodeficiency.
IRF7-related primary immunodeficiency; severe viral infections are separately diagnosed manifestations, not evidence of intrinsic pulmonary damage.
46,XX testicular DSD commonly includes hypergonadotropic gonadal failure; elevated LH/FSH support endocrine involvement beyond reproductive anatomy.
Fibrous replacement of marrow defines the disease; splenic blood-organ involvement remains on this axis; hepatic functional damage is not established as common.
GLIS2-related nephronophthisis causes renal tubular atrophy and progressive kidney failure; no common extrarenal damage is established.
Acid-base disorders belong to the metabolic axis; renal or pulmonary causes cannot be generalized across this umbrella.
Disordered epidermal keratinization defines this skin-disease umbrella.
Inherited intrahepatic bile transport/metabolic disease; extrahepatic damage is not shared across most subtypes.
The syndrome is defined by limb malformations, sensorineural deafness and nail abnormalities; deafness occurs in 4/5 and nail abnormalities in 30-79%.
Colorectal adenomas, osteomas and skin/soft-tissue tumors define Gardner syndrome; retinal pigment lesions generally do not impair vision.
Immune-mediated cutaneous lichen planus with annular atrophic lesions; common mucosal damage is not established for this variant.
Distal tubular acidosis, nephrocalcinosis and intellectual disability define the syndrome; skeletal damage includes scoliosis in 4/4, osteopenia in 3/3 and femoral osteonecrosis in 2/4.
Inherited hepatic porphyrin metabolism disorder with liver-localized UROD dysfunction and blistering skin fragility; cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma are not added as common manifestations.
Benign adipose neoplasm of axillary soft tissue/subcutis; no evidence of origin in muscle or another organ.
Congenital absence of limb skin with residual scarring; limb location does not imply skeletal disease.
Neurodevelopmental disease with delay and seizures; enamel defects occur in 16% and tooth discoloration in 20%; dysphagia reflects neurologic dysfunction rather than direct GI damage.
